runtimeCapability.description: A runtime capability: an opaque secret held by the execution host and stored by the service only as SHA-256. It is bound to one project, executor resource and runtime unit, and it is not a member identity.

mediaBridgeCapability.description: The media bridge's capability: an opaque secret on the bridge host; the API holds only its SHA-256. It names no member and grants no member authority: tool calls act for the speaker the exchange's input epoch binds, under that speaker's own role.

renderRunnerCapability.description: A render runner capability: an opaque secret held by the supervisor on the renderer host; the service stores only its SHA-256. It claims, reads, uploads and settles render jobs under their leases, and nothing else: no member, project or runtime authority.

coordinationCapability.description: The Paperclip dsh adapter's credential: an opaque secret held by the Paperclip service, stored by Sophia only as SHA-256, bound to one Paperclip company. It is not a member identity and not a Paperclip token.

expectedAffected.description: What the member's preview listed, in its order: the version ids, and each decision's id with the revision shown (a decision's revision moves whenever its state changes). Required: the withdrawal erases only if that is still exactly what it reaches, at those revisions, and answers a stale conflict otherwise.

previewToken.description: The preview's proof, as the preview returned it: the server showed this member exactly this list for this note. A list built without a preview, or another member's or note's proof, is refused; an expired one is a stale conflict.

MissionWithdrawalPreview.description: What forgetting this note would erase for everyone, computed by the same rule the withdrawal then applies: the note's versions, from the reader's own earliest wording in its history (an admin's: its first version) to its latest, and every proposal or decision citing any of them. The ledger may move before the member confirms; the withdrawal must send this list back as `expectedAffected` (the version ids, and each decision's id and revision) with this `previewToken`, and answers a stale conflict instead of erasing anything not shown, or in a state not shown.

previewToken.description: The server's proof that it showed this member this list for this note: an HMAC under a key only the database holds, of the member, the project, the note, the expiry and the reach (ids and revisions, never text). The withdrawal must carry it

expiresAt.description: When previewToken stops being accepted: 15 minutes after the preview

entries.description: The note's versions that would be forgotten, oldest first, with their words

epoch.description: Moves with each erasure: a write names the epoch it was made against, and one made against another is refused.

VoiceInputWindowReceipt.description: From the first 16 kHz chunk the bridge forwarded to the provider for the principal until the turn completes, is interrupted, hands off, pauses or closes. pcmSha256Chain covers the PCM forwarded (sha-256-chain-v1); it is never comparable to the Lab's source audio. connection is the durable ordinal its connection's reservation returned.

VoiceInputTurnReceipt.description: The provider's turn for an input window ended. transcriptChars is a count only: no transcript is kept.

VoiceProviderReceipt.description: The provider session's lifecycle and usage, on one reserved connection (connection is the durable ordinal its reservation returned). usageTokens and lastPromptTokens are that connection's own: what the provider reported of its session, which the service keeps as the connection's highest report. connectionsOpened and turns are what the bridge saw; the service's own counts are the reservations'.

VoiceOutputReplyReceipt.description: A reply the bridge played to the room ended. playedSha256Chain covers the 20 ms frames handed to the room track (sha-256-chain-v1). connection is the durable ordinal its connection's reservation returned.

VoiceSessionClosedReceipt.description: The bridge's session for the exchange closed. transcriptRetained is always false.

MediaEvidenceWrite.description: One bridge receipt for an exchange under a grant, by its per-exchange sequence number: the same receipt again is a no-op, another under the same number is refused (409 idempotency_conflict). Only numbers, booleans, enumerated words, ids, digests and times: no free text.

MediaEvidenceAck.description: Whether the exchange has ended, and why (null when it has not): a guard reason, or bridge when the bridge's own bound or the deadline stopped its session (its session_closed receipt said guard).

MediaQualificationReserve.description: The bridge's durable reservation for an exchange under a grant, before it spends: a provider connection before it opens one; a generation before it sends what can start one (input after a turn ended, a tool response, a notice, a typed message), on a reserved connection; or a generation that started unasked (its output arrived), which is counted and charged whatever the limits. charge is the generation's worst case (the context again and its output twice) plus what was sent and transcribed since the connection's last charge.

MediaQualificationReservation.description: Granted, with a connection's durable ordinal (null for a generation), or refused: then the exchange has ended (ended true) and stop says why.

VoiceGuardReceipt.description: Written by the service when its guard ended the exchange (seq 0).

QualificationEvidence.description: What the grant's principal may read of an exchange its grant covers: the grant's limits and what was reserved and reported against them, and the receipts kept (24 hours) in order. Anyone else finds nothing.

connectionsOpened.description: Provider connections reserved for the exchange (durable: only a reservation adds to it).

turns.description: Generations reserved for the exchange, asked for or not (durable: only a reservation adds to it).

usageTokens.description: What the provider reported, each reserved connection's highest report, summed.

committedTokens.description: What the exchange may have cost: each reserved connection at the greater of what was charged to it (each generation at its worst case) and what the provider reported of it, summed. The guard holds this to the budget.

lastPromptTokens.description: The prompt size the exchange's latest connection last reported.

RoomLivePresence.description: The room as the media bridge last saw it, for a member: whether the caller is in it, how many people are and how many of them are guests, the bridge's voice and the report's age. Nobody else's identity. observed false (no report) or fresh false (older than 15 s; the bridge reports every 5 s while it is in the room) proves nothing either way.

ExchangeCalls.description: A member's own voice tool calls in an exchange, in the order the service recorded them (seq, increasing across all exchanges), each with the tool it named, the command it admitted, the task that command created, and when and how the API answered it. Only calls of a voice qualification grant's principal, in an exchange opened under that grant, are recorded. command is null for a call that admitted nothing (a read, a clarification, a refusal: a Hold on work that is not running admits no command; a repeat answered with the task under way) and for one not answered yet (answeredAt null: whatever it admits may not have committed). A replayed call is its first call's one entry. A command is the call's only when the transaction that inserted it did so for this call; a member's own command under the call's key is not. Another member's calls and another exchange's are never listed. readAt is when this was read: given back as after, only calls whose recording began after that read are listed, so a call already on its way at that read, committed or not, never is.
